question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the roots of $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-x+2}{3x-3}$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}} $\,$
and
$\,\,x=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-x+2}{3x-3}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-x+2}{3x-3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}(x-2)-1(x-2)}{3x-3} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}-1)(x-2)}{3(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)}{3(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(x-1)}(x+1)(x-2)}{3\cancel{(x-1)}} \\  & =\frac{(x+1)(x-2)}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-1,\,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $f(x)=0$, in ascending order, are $x=-1$ and $x=2.$
